body:
Split out of task:fd4acc7182802a8f (its tech-debt note 2; the investigation's recommendation is in its note 5).

### Problem

When a Rust `extract` moves tests into `<module>_tests.rs`, `extract::rust.ancestor_glob_needed` decides per **name**, not per **glob**. If an ancestor module has several globs and any needed name might come from one of them, every glob in that ancestor is carried. The unused ones show up as unused-import warnings in the new test file.

The store alone can't tell which external glob supplies a name (for example `std::fmt::*` vs `std::collections::*` for `BTreeSet`), so only the compiler can decide.

### Required

- Keep `ancestor_glob_needed`'s current per-name check as the first filter.
- After the move, drop any glob that the extract itself carried into `<module>_tests.rs` and that cargo reports as an unused import. Never touch imports the user wrote.
- Reuse the diagnostics the move already gets: `rust_check.post_move_check` calls `check_all`, which returns warnings as well as errors (`Diag.error` is false for a warning). Avoid a second cargo run if that's workable.
- The cleanup write goes through the same rollback as the move: if it fails, nothing changes.

### Acceptance

- New test: root has `use std::fmt::*;` and `use std::collections::*;`; the moved test uses only `BTreeSet`. `helpers_tests.rs` has `std::collections::*` but no `std::fmt::*`, and `check_all` returns no messages.
- `a_used_ancestor_glob_moves_with_tests` and `an_unused_ancestor_glob_stays_out_of_moved_tests` still pass.
- `check --warnings` is clean.

### Risks

- A glob unused under one `cfg` but used under another.
- A test-only glob cargo sees only when building tests: make sure the diagnostics used cover the test target.
title: extract: drop unused carried ancestor globs
